# Time Series Forecasting

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-time-series-forecasting/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-time-series-forecasting/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How to forecast demand a day ahead and check that the forecast holds up: baselines, backtests that never see the future, statistical models, one LightGBM model for all clients, totals that add up, and calibrated prediction intervals, on hourly electricity demand from thirty clients.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For data scientists and analysts who know pandas and basic regression and are asked to forecast demand, such as sales, energy, tickets or traffic, and need forecasts that hold up when they are checked.

## Contents

| | Chapter | By the end, you can | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Forecast tomorrow's demand](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/forecast-tomorrows-demand) · [source](chapters/01-forecast-tomorrows-demand.md) | This chapter builds the first forecast of tomorrow's demand, and the simple baseline that every later forecast has to beat | 3 |
| 2 | [Set the baselines a model must beat](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/beat-the-naive-baselines) · [source](chapters/02-set-the-baselines.md) | In this chapter you compute three baselines for a client's day-ahead forecast, naive, seasonal naive and average of weeks, and scale a client's error with MASE, using a scale that reads only the readings before the forecast week | 2 |
| 3 | [Backtest without looking ahead](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/backtest-without-looking-ahead) · [source](chapters/03-backtest-without-looking-ahead.md) | This chapter teaches you to score a day-ahead forecast over a year of cutoffs without letting the future into its history, to handle the two clock-change hours in the data, and to run a shift test that catches a feature which reads past its cutoff | 7 |
| 4 | [Fit a statistical model for each client](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/fit-statistical-models-per-client) · [source](chapters/04-fit-statistical-models.md) | Here you fit AutoETS and a fixed seasonal ARIMA for each client over the same backtest, score both against seasonal naive, and learn to start a late-starting client at its first reading | 6 |
| 5 | [Add calendar and lag features](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/add-calendar-and-lag-features) · [source](chapters/05-calendar-and-lag-features.md) | After this chapter, you can turn one client's hourly history into a feature table, add lags and calendar and holiday features that a day-ahead forecast is allowed to see, measure what each feature adds on the same windows, and catch a lag that reads the day being forecast | 2 |
| 6 | [Forecast many clients with one model](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/forecast-many-clients-at-once) · [source](chapters/06-many-clients-one-model.md) | You finish this chapter with one global model for all thirty clients, a start rule that keeps the late starters' leading zeros out of it, and a score that sets it beside seasonal naive for each client on the same cutoffs | 4 |
| 7 | [Make the total add up](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/make-the-total-add-up) · [source](chapters/07-totals-that-add-up.md) | You'll forecast the total demand of thirty clients two ways, choose between the two on decision windows, and split that total into client shares using only the history before each cutoff | 2 |
| 8 | [Quantify forecast uncertainty](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/quantify-forecast-uncertainty) · [source](chapters/08-uncertainty.md) | This chapter puts a range around each day-ahead forecast, so you can say whether a purchase can rely on it | 4 |
| 9 | [Compare Prophet and a foundation model](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/compare-prophet-and-a-foundation-model) · [source](chapters/09-compare-prophet-and-a-foundation-model.md) | Once you finish this chapter, you can fit Prophet on the book's three standard cutoffs, load a recorded foundation model (Chronos-2) and a recorded neural model (NHITS), and score all of them on one MASE scale against the same readings | 6 |
| 10 | [Keep the forecast running](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/keep-the-forecast-running) · [source](chapters/10-keep-the-forecast-running.md) | Once a forecast runs every day, the question changes from whether it scored well to whether it still holds on the day it's used | 5 |

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.13.16
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python load-lead-client.py
```

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, the examples that use it run again in the new version, and every example runs again each week. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/changes).
